title: Stabilize CUDA graph replay + cross-version fallback manager for mixed Triton runtimes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We are seeing nondeterministic failures and tail-latency spikes when replaying CUDA graphs across heterogeneous customer fleets running different Triton/CUDA/CUTLASS stacks. Root causes identified in triage: (1) mismatched stream/invoke conventions between Triton versions that change kernel launch ordering under CUDA graph replay, (2) a thin kernel-signature adapter that assumes identical symbol layouts across CUTLASS variants, and (3) insufficient synchronization when falling back from a graph-optimized path to a legacy kernel path.

Goal: Implement a version-adaptive fallback manager and refactor the graph-replay orchestration to ensure correct ordering, robust symbol resolution across CUTLASS variants, and predictable performance when falling back. This should reduce incorrect outputs, remove rare crashes during replay, and eliminate the observed 5-15% tail-latency regressions under mixed-version fleets.

Design/Approach:
- Introduce "Fallback Manager" abstraction in the runtime submit path that: (a) probes the runtime capability matrix on startup; (b) selects a replay strategy (direct graph, graph+shim, or non-graph) per-device based on driver/Triton/CUTLASS signatures; (c) encapsulates safe fallback transitions with explicit quiesce/sync points.
- Replace the existing ad-hoc signature checks with a normalized kernel metadata registry (lightweight string mapping) that tolerates symbol renames and missing optional kernels by preferring compatible alternatives with explicit feature flags.
- Add a small synchronization barrier inside the replay hotpath that is a no-op on modern drivers but prevents ordering regressions on older Triton variants. Controlled by runtime feature flag and canary.
- Expand CI matrix to run graph-replay integration tests against CUDA 11.8/12.x/13.x + Triton 2.x/3.x combinations using mocked devices in our infra and a small hardware smoke pool for real-device verification.
- Telemetry: emit a replay_strategy tag and a fallback_count metric per invocation to monitor field behavior and regressions.

Trade-offs and Risks:
- Introducing additional runtime checks and a quiesce barrier can add a small constant cost to fast-paths. We will gate rollout with feature flags and only enable the barrier for fleets that need it.
- The kernel metadata registry must be kept up-to-date as we onboard new CUTLASS builds; this introduces maintenance cost but avoids brittle symbol probing at runtime.
- Rolling this across Dedicated/Private fleets requires a staged canary to avoid impacting high-SLA customers.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Repro cases from GH issue #4526 show deterministic success across targeted driver/Triton combos in the smoke pool.
2) Tail latency (95/99) regressions observed in affected workloads reduced to within 2% of baseline after canary (measured in runtime-1.24 canary).
3) Fallback_count telemetry is available in Console and dashboard panels for rollout monitoring.
4) Unit and integration tests added to CI for the new strategies.

Deliverables:
- RFC design doc linked in attachments.
- Implementation of Fallback Manager, kernel metadata registry, and optional barrier.
- CI matrix expansion + smoke-pool test runs.
- Canaried rollout plan and runbook for rollback.

Notes: This ticket intentionally avoids broad kernel engine rewrites; the aim is surgical stabilization and observability to unblock customers while a larger kernel-selection refactor is incubated in a follow-up epic.
